facts.claim: Selection bias in favor of male over female candidates was eliminated and, if anything, slightly reversed in sign starting in 2009 for mixed-gender and male-stereotypical jobs in our sample.

facts.claim: Hiring discrimination against candidates with disabilities, older candidates, and less physically attractive candidates seems equally severe as the unequal treatment of candidates with salient racial or ethnic characteristics.

facts.claim: In high-discrimination countries, white natives receive nearly twice the callbacks of nonwhites; in low-discrimination countries, white natives receive about 25 percent more.
facts.quote: In high-discrimination countries, white natives receive nearly twice the callbacks of nonwhites; in low-discrimination countries, white natives receive about 25 percent more.

facts.claim: Since 1989, whites receive on average 36% more callbacks than African Americans, and 24% more callbacks than Latinos.

facts.claim: Discrimination is significantly greater in the selection process for low-skilled than for high-skilled jobs.

research.angle: While some gender biases have been eliminated or reversed, hiring discrimination based on race, age, disability, and physical attractiveness remains severe and varies significantly by country and job skill level.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that names and characteristics associated with race, age, and disability continue to result in fewer callbacks for many applicants.
research.caveat: The studies show that the level of discrimination varies significantly depending on the specific country, job type, and the amount of positive information provided in the application.
